en: I have a billion and one questions for you.

en: I'm really excited to be chatting.

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to start with something that's very timely, something that's happening this week.
zh: 我想从一件非常及时的事情开始,一件本周正在发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something that's in the news right now is this whole Zuck coming after all the top AI researchers offering them $100 million signing bonuses, $100 million comp.
zh: 眼下新闻里的一件事就是 Zuck 挖角所有顶级 AI 研究员,给他们提供 1 亿美元签约奖金,1 亿美元薪酬。

en: He's poaching from all the top AI labs.

en: I imagine this something you're dealing with.
zh: 我想这这是你正在处理的事情。

en: I'm just curious, what are you seeing inside Anthropic and just what's your take on the strategy?
zh: 我只是好奇,你在 Anthropic 内部看到了什么,你对这个策略有什么看法?

speaker: Unknown
en: Where do you think things go from here?
zh: 你认为事情从这里会走向何方?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean I think this is a sign of the times.
zh: 是的,我认为这是一个时代的标志。

speaker: Unknown
en: The technology that we're developing is extremely valuable.
zh: 我们正在开发的技术非常有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our company is growing super, super fast.
zh: 我们公司增长超级超级快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many of the other companies in the space are growing really fast.
zh: 这个领域的许多其他公司也增长非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at Anthropic, I think we've been maybe much less affected than many of the other companies in the space because people here are so mission oriented and they stay because... They get these offers and then they say, "Well, of course I'm not going to leave because my best case scenario at Meta is that we make money and my best case at Anthropic is we affect the future of humanity and try to make AI flourish and human flourishing go well."
zh: 在 Anthropic,我认为我们受到的影响可能比这个领域的许多其他公司要小得多,因为这里的人非常以使命为导向,他们留下来是因为……他们收到了这些offer,然后他们说,“当然,我不会离开,因为我在 Meta 的最好情况是我们赚钱,而我在 Anthropic 的最好情况是我们影响人类的未来并试图让 AI 繁荣和人类繁荣发展得很好。”

speaker: Unknown
en: To me, it's not a hard choice.
zh: 对我来说,这不难选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: Other people have different life circumstances and it makes it a much harder decision for them.
zh: 其他人有不同的生活境况,这使得这对他们来说是一个更艰难的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: For anybody who does get those mega offers and accepts them, I can't say I hold it against them when they accept it, but it's definitely not something that I would want to take myself if it came to me.
zh: 对于任何收到这些超级offer并接受它们的人,当他们接受时我不能说我不怪他们,但这绝对不是如果轮到我我会想要自己接受的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to talk about a lot of this stuff that you've mentioned.
zh: 我们将讨论你提到的很多事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: In terms of the offers do you think, is this a real number that you're seeing this $100 million signing bonus, is that a real thing?
zh: 关于这些offer,你认为,这是你看到的真实数字吗,这个 1 亿美元签约奖金,那是真的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know if you've actually seen that.
zh: 我不知道你是否真的见过那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm pretty sure it's real.
zh: 我很确定它是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you just think about the amount of impact that individuals can have on a company's trajectory, in our case, we are selling hotcakes and if we get a 1 or 10 or 5% efficiency bonus on our inference stack, that is worth an incredible amount of money.
zh: 如果你只是想想个人对公司轨迹可能产生的影响,在我们的案例中,我们的产品卖得像热蛋糕,如果我们的推理堆栈获得 1% 或 10% 或 5% 的效率提升,那是值得难以置信的金钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so to pay individuals like $100 million over four year package, that's actually pretty cheap compared to the value created for the business.
zh: 因此支付个人像 1 亿美元的四年的方案,相比于为业务创造的价值,这实际上是相当便宜的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're just in an unprecedented era of scale and it's only going to get crazier actually.
zh: 我认为我们正处于一个规模空前并且只会变得疯狂的时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you extrapolate the exponential on how much companies are spending, it's like 2X a year roughly in terms of CapEx, and today we're maybe in the globally $300 billion range, the entire industry spending on this, and so numbers like 100 million are a drop in the bucket.
zh: 如果你对公司的支出呈指数级推演,大约每年2倍,按照 CapEx,如今我们可能在全球 3000 亿美元范围内,整个行业在这个上面花费,所以像 1 亿这样的数字只是九牛一毛。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you go a few years out, a couple more doublings, we're talking about trillions of dollars and at that point it's just really hard to think about these numbers.
zh: 但如果你再过几年,再多几次翻倍,我们谈论的是万亿美元,在那时真的很难思考这些数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: Along these lines, something that a lot of people feel with AI progress is that we're hitting plateaus in many ways that it feels like newer models are just not as smart as previous leaps.
zh: 沿着这些思路,许多人对 AI 进展的感觉是我们在许多方面正在触及平台期,感觉更新的模型不像以前飞跃那么聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I know you don't believe this.
zh: 但我知道你不相信这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know you don't believe that we've hit plateaus on scaling loss.
zh: 我知道你不相信我们在缩放损失上触及了平台期。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about just what you're seeing there and what you think people are missing.
zh: 谈谈你在那里看到的以及你认为人们错过了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of funny because this narrative comes out every six months or so and it's never been true, and so I kind of wish people would have a little bit of a bullshit detector in their heads when they see this.
zh: 这有点好笑,因为这个叙事每六个月左右出现一次,而且从未成真,所以我有点希望人们看到它时脑子里能有一个废话探测器。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think progress has actually been accelerating where if you look at the cadence of model releases, it used to be once a year and now with the improvements in our post-training techniques, we're seeing releases every month or three months, and so I would say progress is actually accelerating in many ways, but there's this weird time compression effect.
zh: 我认为进展实际上正在加速,如果你看看模型发布的节奏,它曾经是一年一次,现在随着我们在后训练技术上的改进,我们看到每个月或三个月发布一次,所以我认为进展在许多方面实际上正在加速,但有一种奇怪的时间压缩效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dario compared it to being in a near light speed journey where a day that passes for you is like five days back on earth and we're accelerating.
zh: Dario 把它比作接近光速的旅程,你度过的一天就像地球上的五天,我们正在加速。

speaker: Unknown
en: The time dilation is increasing.
zh: 时间膨胀正在增加。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's part of what's causing people to say that progress is slowing down, but if you look at the scaling laws, they're continuing to hold true.
zh: 我认为这也是导致人们说进展正在放缓的部分原因,但如果你看看缩放定律,它们继续成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: We did kind of need this transition from normal pre-training to reinforcement learning scaling up to continue the scaling laws, but I think it's kind of like for semiconductors where it's less about the density of transistors that you can fit on a chip and more about how many flops can you fit in a data center or something.
zh: 我们确实需要这种从普通预训练到强化学习的扩展的转变来保持缩放定律,但我认为这有点像半导体,与其说是你能装在芯片上的晶体管密度,不如说是你能装在数据中心里的浮点运算数量之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to change the definition around a little bit to keep your eye on the prize.
zh: 你必须稍微改变一下定义才能保持关注目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, this is one of the few phenomena in the world that has held across so many orders of magnitude.
zh: 但是是的,这是世界上少数几个跨越如此多个数量级都成立的现象之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually pretty surprising that it is continuing to hold.
zh: 它实际上相当令人惊讶,它继续成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: To me, if you look at fundamental laws of physics, many of them don't hold across 15 orders of magnitude, so it's pretty surprising.
zh: 对我来说，如果你看物理的基本定律，其中许多并不跨越 15 个数量级都成立，所以这非常令人惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: It boggles the the mind.
zh: 这让人难以理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you're saying essentially is we're seeing newer models being released more often, and so we're comparing it to the last version and we're just not seeing as much advance.
zh: 你所说的基本上是，我们看到新模型更频繁地发布，所以我们将其与上一版本进行比较，而我们只是没有看到那么多的进步。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you go back and it was like a model released once a year, it was a huge leap, and so people are missing that.
zh: 但如果你回过头，就像是一年发布一次模型，那是巨大的飞跃，所以人们怀念那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're just seeing many more iterations.
zh: 我们只是看到了更多的迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess, to be a little bit more generous to the people saying things are slowing down.
zh: 我猜，稍微对那些说事情正在放缓的人宽容一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that for some tasks we are saturating the amount of intelligence needed for that task, maybe to extract information from a simple document that already has form fields on it or something like it's just so easy that okay, yeah, we're already at 100% and there's this great chart on Our World in Data that shows that when you release a new benchmark within six to 12 months, it immediately gets saturated.
zh: 我认为对于某些任务，我们正在达到该任务所需的智能饱和度，也许是从一个已经有表格字段的简单文档中提取信息或类似的事情，它太容易了，以至于好吧，是的，我们已经达到了 100%，并且 Our World in Data 上有一张很棒的图表显示，当你发布一个新的基准测试时，在 6 到 12 个月内，它就会立即饱和。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so maybe the real constraint is how can we come up with better benchmarks and better ambition of using the tools that then reveals the bumps in intelligence that we're seeing now.
zh: 所以也许真正的约束在于，我们如何想出更好的基准测试和更好的使用工具的雄心，从而揭示我们现在看到的智能 bumps。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a good segue to you have a very specific way of thinking about AGI and defining what AGI means.
zh: 这是一个很好的过渡，你对 AGI 有一种非常具体的思考方式和定义 AGI 的含义。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think AGI is kind of a loaded term, and so I tend not to use it very much anymore internally.
zh: 我认为 AGI 是一个有点 loaded 的术语，所以我倾向于在内部不再经常使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead, I like the term transformative AI because it's less about can it do as much as people do?
zh: 相反，我喜欢 transformative AI 这个术语，因为它更多的是关于它是否像人们做的那样多？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can it do literally everything and more about objectively is it causing transformation in society and the economy?
zh: 它是否能在字面上做所有事情，而更多的是关于客观上它是否正在引起社会和经济的转变？

speaker: Unknown
en: A very concrete way of measuring that is the Economic Turing Test.
zh: 有一个非常具体的衡量方法是 Economic Turing Test。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't come up with this, but I really like it.
zh: 我不是想出这个的人，但我真的很喜欢它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's this idea that if you contract an agent for a month or three months on a particular job, if you decide to hire that agent and it turns out to be a machine rather than a person, then it's passed the Economic Turing Test for that role.
zh: 这个想法是，如果你为一个特定工作雇佣一个 agent 一个月或三个月，如果你决定雇佣那个 agent 并且结果证明那是一台机器而不是一个人，那么它就通过了该角色的 Economic Turing Test。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you can sort of expand that out in the same way that for measuring purchasing power parity or inflation, there's a basket of goods.
zh: 然后你可以以同样的方式将其扩展，就像衡量购买力平价或通货膨胀一样，有一篮子商品。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can have a market basket of jobs, and if the agent can pass the Economic Turing Test for 50% of money-weighted jobs, then we have transformative AI and the exact thresholds don't really matter that much, but it's kind of illustrative to say if we pass that threshold, then we would expect massive effects on world GDP increases and societal change and how many people are employed and things like that because societal institutions and organizations are sticky, it's slow to have change, but once these things are possible you know that it's the start of a new era.
zh: 你可以有一篮子的工作，如果 agent 能够通过 50% 的 money-weighted 工作的 Economic Turing Test，那么我们就拥有了 transformative AI，确切的阈值并不那么重要，但它可以说是说明性的，如果我们通过那个阈值，那么我们将预期对世界 GDP 增长和社会变革以及有多少人受雇等方面产生巨大影响，因为社会制度和组织是 sticky，变革很慢，但一旦这些事情成为可能，你知道这是一个新时代的开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Along these lines, Dario, your CO recently talked about how AI is going to take a huge part of, I don't know, half of white-collar jobs, that unemployment might go up to something like 20%.
zh: 沿着这些思路，Dario，你的 CO 最近谈到了 AI 将占据……我不知道……白领工作的一半，失业率可能会上升到 20% 左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know you're even more vocal and opinionated about just how much impact AI is already having in the workplace that people may not even be realizing.
zh: 我知道你对 AI 已经在工作场所产生了多大的影响更加直言不讳和固执己见，人们甚至可能没有意识到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about just what you think people are missing about the impact AI is going to have on jobs and is already having.
zh: 谈谈你认为人们对 AI 将对工作产生的影响以及已经产生的影响所缺少的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so from an economic standpoint, there's a couple different kinds of unemployment, and one is because the workers just don't have the skills to do the kinds of jobs that the economy needs.
zh: 是的，所以从经济角度来看，有几种不同的失业，一种是因为工人根本没有经济所需工作类型的技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And another kind is where those jobs are just completely eliminated, and I think it's going to be actually a combination of these things, but if you just think about 20 years in the future where we're way past the singularity, it's hard for me to imagine that even capitalism will look at all it looks today.
zh: 另一种是那些工作被完全消除，我认为这实际上是这些事情的组合，但如果你只是想象 20 年后的未来，我们远远 past 了奇点，很难想象资本主义会看起来和今天一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we do our jobs, we will have safe aligned superintelligence, we'll have, as Dario says, in Machines of Love and Grace, a country of geniuses in a data center, and the ability to accelerate positive change in science, technology, education, mathematics, it's going to be amazing.
zh: 如果我们做好我们的工作，我们将拥有 safe aligned superintelligence，我们将拥有，正如 Dario 在《Machines of Love and Grace》中所说，数据中心里的天才之国，以及加速科学、技术、教育、数学积极变化的能力，这将是非常棒的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that also means in a world of abundance where labor is almost free and anything you want to do, you can just ask an expert to do for you, then what do jobs even look like?
zh: 但这也意味着在一个丰富的世界里，劳动力几乎是免费的，你想做的任何事情，你都可以请专家为你做，那么工作看起来像什么呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I guess there's this scary transition period from where we are today where people have jobs and capitalism works and the world of 20 years from now where everything is completely different, but part of the reason they call it the singularity is that it's a point beyond which you can't easily forecast what's going to happen.
zh: 所以我想有一个可怕的过渡时期，从今天人们有工作、资本主义运作的世界，到 20 年后一切完全不同的世界，但他们称之为奇点的部分原因是，这是你无法轻易预测未来会发生什么的点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just such a fast rate of change and so different that it's hard to even imagine.
zh: 变化的速度如此之快，如此不同，甚至很难想象。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess taking the view from the limit, it's pretty easy to say hopefully we'll have figured it out.
zh: 我想从极限的角度来看，很容易说希望我们会弄明白的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in a world of abundance, maybe the jobs themselves, it's not that scary, and I think making sure that that transition time goes well is pretty important.
zh: 在一个丰富的世界里，也许工作本身并不可怕，我认为确保那个过渡时期进展顺利非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a couple of threads I want to follow there.
zh: 我想接着那几点跟进。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is people hear this, there's a lot of headlines around this.
zh: 一个是人们听到这个，有很多关于这个的新闻标题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most people probably don't actually feel this yet or see this happening and so there's always this, I guess, I don't know, maybe, but I don't know it's hard to believe, my job seems fine.
zh: 大多数人可能实际上还没有感觉到这一点或看到这一点发生，所以总是有这种，我想，我不知道，也许，但我不知道这很难相信，我的工作看起来很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nothing's changed.
zh: 什么都没有改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you seeing just happening today already that you think people don't see or misunderstand in terms of the impact AI is having on jobs?
zh: 你今天看到正在发生的事情，你认为人们看不到或误解了 AI 对工作的影响？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think part of this is that people are really bad at modeling exponential progress.
zh: 我认为部分原因是人们真的很不擅长建模指数级进步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you look at an exponential on a graph, it looks flat and almost zero at the beginning of it, and then suddenly you hit the knee of the curve and things are changing real fast and then it goes vertical.
zh: 如果你看看图表上的指数曲线，它在一开始看起来是平坦的，几乎为零，然后突然你撞到了曲线的拐点，事物变化得非常快，然后它就垂直了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the plot that we've been on for a long time.
zh: 这是我们长期以来一直处于的曲线。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess I started feeling it in 2019 maybe when GPT-2 came out and I was like, "Oh, this is how we're going to get to AGI."
zh: 我想我大概在 2019 年开始感觉到这一点，当时 GPT-2 出来了，我想，"哦，这就是我们要达到 AGI 的方式。"

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that was pretty early compared to a lot of people where when they saw ChatGPT, they were like, "Wow, something is different and changing."
zh: 但我认为这比很多人要早，当他们看到 ChatGPT 时，他们会想，"哇，有些事情不同了并且在改变。"

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I guess I wouldn't expect widespread transformation in a lot of parts of society, and I would expect this skepticism reaction.
zh: 所以我想我不会预期社会许多部分发生广泛的转变，我会预期这种怀疑的反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's very reasonable and it's exactly what is the standard linear view of progress.
zh: 我认为这是非常合理的，这确实是标准的线性进步观。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I guess to cite a couple of areas where I think things are changing quite quickly.
zh: 但我想引用几个我认为变化很快的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: In customer service we're seeing with things like Fin and Intercom, they're a great partner of ours, 82% customer service resolution rates automatically without a human involved.
zh: 在客户服务方面，我们看到像 Fin 和 Intercom 这样的东西，他们是我们的绝佳合作伙伴，82% 的客户服务解决率是自动的，没有人类参与。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in terms of software engineering, our Claude Code team, like 95% of the code is written by Claude.
zh: 在软件工程方面，我们的 Claude Code 团队，比如 95% 的代码是由 Claude 编写的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think a different way to phrase that is that we write 10X more code or 20X more code, and so a much, much smaller team can just be much, much more impactful.
zh: 但我想换种说法是，我们编写的代码多 10 倍或 20 倍，所以一个非常非常小的团队可以产生非常非常大的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And similarly for the customer service, yes, you can phrase it as 82% customer service resolution rates, but that nets out in the humans doing those tasks, able to focus on the harder parts of those tasks.
zh: 同样对于客户服务，是的，你可以说它是 82% 的客户服务解决率，但结果是那些做这些任务的人类能够专注于这些任务中更难的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for the more tricky situations that in a normal world like five years ago, they would've had to just drop those tickets because it was too much effort for them to actually go do the investigation.
zh: 对于更棘手的情况，在像五年前的正常世界里，他们不得不放弃这些工单，因为对他们来说实际去调查太费劲了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were too many other tickets for them to worry about.
zh: 有太多其他的工单需要他们担心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in the immediate term, there will be a massive expansion of the pie and the amount of labor that people can do.
zh: 我认为在短期内，馅饼和人们能做的劳动量将会有巨大的扩张。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've never met a hiring manager at a growth company and heard them say, "I don't want to hire more people."
zh: 我在一家成长型公司从未遇到过招聘经理并听到他们说，"我不想雇佣更多的人。"

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the hopeful version of it.
zh: 那是充满希望的版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: But with things that are lower skill jobs or less headroom on how good they can be, I think there will be a lot of displacement.
zh: 但对于那些低技能工作或者它们能做好的空间有限的事情，我认为会有很多的取代。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is just something we as a society need to get ahead of and work on.
zh: 这是我们作为一个社会需要未雨绸缪并努力解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to talk more about that, but something that I also want to help people with is how do they get a leg up in this future world?
zh: 我想多聊聊这一点，但我也想帮助人们的一点是，他们如何在这个未来的世界中脱颖而出？

speaker: Unknown
en: They listen to this, they're like, "Oh, this doesn't sound great.
zh: 他们听到这个，他们会想，“哦，这听起来不太好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I need to think ahead."
zh: 我需要提前思考。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I know you won't have all the answers, but just do you have any advice for folks that want to try to get ahead of this and kind of future-proof their career and their life to not be replaced by AI?
zh: 我知道你不会拥有所有答案，但你对那些想要尝试未雨绸缪并想要保障他们的事业和生活不被 AI 取代的人有什么建议吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything you've seen people do, anything you recommend they start trying to do more of?
zh: 你看到人们做过什么，你有什么建议是他们开始尝试多做的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Even for me and being in the center of a lot of this transformation, I'm not immune to job replacement either.
zh: 即使对于我，身处很多这种转变的中心，我也不能免于被工作取代。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just some vulnerability there of at some point it's coming for all of us.
zh: 只是展示一些脆弱性，在某个时刻它正在向我们所有人走来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even you, Ben, now.
zh: 包括你，Ben，现在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you, Lenny.
zh: 还有你，Lenny。

speaker: Lenny
en: And me.
zh: 还有我。

speaker: Benjamin Mann
en: Sorry.
zh: 抱歉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, wait, we've gone too far now.
zh: 哦，等等，我们现在走得太远了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in terms of the transition period, yeah, I think there are things that we can do, and I think a big part of it is just being ambitious and how you use the tools and being willing to learn new tools.
zh: 但就过渡时期而言，是的，我认为我们可以做一些事情，我认为其中很大一部分就是要有雄心壮志以及你如何使用这些工具，并愿意学习新工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: People who use the new tools as if they were old tools tend to not succeed.
zh: 那些像使用旧工具一样使用新工具的人往往不会成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: As an example of that, when you're coding, people are very familiar with autocomplete, people are familiar with SimpleChat where they can ask questions about the code base, but the difference between people who use Claude Code very effectively and people who use it not so effectively is like are they asking for the ambitious change?
zh: 作为一个例子，当你在编码时，人们很熟悉自动补全，人们很熟悉 SimpleChat，在那里他们可以询问关于代码库的问题，但有效使用 Claude Code 的人和不太有效使用它的人之间的区别在于，他们是否要求雄心勃勃的改变？

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it doesn't work the first time, asking three more times because our success rate when you just completely start over and try again is much, much higher than if you just try once and then just keep banging on the same thing that didn't work.
zh: 如果它第一次不起作用，再问三次，因为当你完全重新开始并再试一次时，我们的成功率比你只尝试一次然后继续在同一个不起作用的事情上敲打要高得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even though that's a coding example and coding is one of the areas that's taking off most dramatically, we have seen internally that our legal team and our finance team are getting a ton of value out of using Claude Code itself.
zh: 尽管这是一个编码的例子，而编码是起飞最显着的领域之一，但我们在内部看到我们的法律团队和我们的财务团队正在从使用 Claude Code 本身获得巨大的价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to be making better interfaces so that they will have an easier time and require a little bit less jumping in the deep end of using Claude Code in the terminal.
zh: 我们将制作更好的界面，这样他们会有更轻松的时光，并且需要少一点跳进使用终端中的 Claude Code 的深水区。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, we're seeing them use it to redline documents and use it to run BigQuery analyses of our customers and our revenue metrics.
zh: 但是是的，我们看到他们用它来红线文档，并使用它来运行关于我们的客户和我们的收入指标的 BigQuery 分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess it's about taking that risk and even if it feels like a scary thing, trying it out.
zh: 我想这是关于承担那个风险，即使它感觉像是一件可怕的事情，也要尝试它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so the advice here is use the tools.
zh: 好的，所以这里的建议是使用工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's something everyone's always saying, just actually use these tools.
zh: 这是每个人一直在说的事情，只是真正使用这些工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like sit in Claude Code.
zh: 它就像是坐在 Claude Code 里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And your point about being more ambitious than you naturally feel like being because maybe it'll actually accomplish the thing.
zh: 你关于要比你自然感觉到的更有雄心的观点，因为也许它实际上会完成那件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: This tip of trying it three times so the idea there is it may not get it right the first time.
zh: 尝试它三次这个技巧，所以那里的想法是它可能第一次没有做对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is the tip there ask it in different ways or is it just try harder, try again?
zh: 那里的技巧是以不同的方式问它，还是只是更努力地尝试，再试一次？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean you can just literally ask the exact same question.
zh: 是的，我的意思是你真的可以问完全相同的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: These things are stochastic and sometimes they'll figure it out and sometimes they won't.
zh: 这些东西是随机的，有时他们会弄明白，有时他们不会。

speaker: Unknown
en: In every one of these model cards, it always shows pass it one versus pass it in.
zh: 在每一个这些模型卡片中，它总是显示 pass it one 对比 pass it in。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's exactly the thing where they try the exact same prompt, sometimes it gets it, sometimes it doesn't.
zh: 而这正是那种他们尝试完全相同的提示的事情，有时他们得到了，有时他们没有得到。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the dumbest advice.
zh: 这是最愚蠢的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I think if you want to be a little bit smarter about it, there can be gains there of saying, "Here's what you already tried and it didn't work, so don't try that.
zh: 但是是的，我认为如果你想关于它更聪明一点，那里可以有一些收获，说，“这是你已经尝试过的并且没有奏效，所以不要尝试那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Try something different."
zh: 尝试一些不同的东西。”

speaker: Unknown
en: That can also help.
zh: 那也可以帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: The advice is comes back to something that a lot of people talk about these days is you won't be replaced by AI at least anytime soon you'll be replaced by someone that is very good using AI?
zh: 这建议回到了如今很多人谈论的一件事，就是你不会很快被 AI 取代，至少很快不会，你会被一个非常擅长使用 AI 的人取代？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in that area it's more like your team will just do dramatically more stuff.
zh: 我认为在那个领域，更像是你的团队只会做戏剧性更多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're definitely not slowing down on hiring at all, and some people are confused by that.
zh: 我们绝对根本没有在招聘上放缓，有些人对此感到困惑。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even in an onboarding class, somebody asked that and they were like, "Why did you hire me if we're all just going to be replaced?"
zh: 甚至在一次入职培训课上，有人问了这个，他们说，“如果我们都要被取代，你为什么要雇佣我？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And the answer is the next couple of years are really critical to get right and we're not at the point where we're doing complete replacement.
zh: 答案是接下来的几年对于做对真的非常关键，而且我们还没到我们要做完全取代的地步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I said, we're still at that flat zero looking part of the exponential compared to where we will be.
zh: 就像我说的，我们仍然处在那个扁平零相对于我们将要处于的指数的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is super important to have great people and that's why we're hiring super aggressively.
zh: 拥有优秀的人超级重要，这就是为什么我们在超级积极地招聘。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me take another approach to asking this question something ask everyone that's at the very cutting edge of where AI is going.
zh: 让我用另一种方法来问这个问题，询问每一个都处于 AI 发展的最前沿的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have kids, knowing what you know about where AI is heading and all these things you've been talking about, what are you focusing on teaching your kids to help them thrive in this AI future?
zh: 你有孩子，知道你所知道的关于 AI 的走向以及你一直在谈论的所有这些事情，你专注于教你的孩子什么来帮助他们在这种 AI 未来中茁壮成长？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I have two daughters, a one-year-old and a three-year-old, so it's pretty in the basics still.
zh: 是的，我有两个女儿，一个一岁和一个三岁，所以它仍然非常基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our three-year-old is now capable of just conversing with Alexa Plus and asking her to explain stuff and play music for her and all that stuff.
zh: 我们的三岁孩子现在能够只是与 Alexa Plus 对话并让她解释东西并为她的播放音乐以及所有那些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's been loving that.
zh: 她一直很喜欢那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I guess more broadly, she goes to a Montessori school and I just love the focus on curiosity and creativity and self-led learning that Montessori has.
zh: 但我想更广泛地说，她去了一所蒙特梭利学校，我只是喜欢蒙特梭利所拥有的对好奇心、创造力和自主学习的关注。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess if I were in a normal era like 10, 20 years ago and I had a kid, maybe I would be trying to line her up for going to a top tier school and doing all the extracurriculars and all that stuff.
zh: 我想如果我在一个正常的时代，比如 10 年或 20 年前，并且我有个孩子，也许我会试图让她进入顶尖学校，做所有的课外活动和所有那些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But at this point, I don't think any of it's going to matter.
zh: 但在这一点上，我不认为这些会有什么意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just want her to be happy and thoughtful and curious and kind.
zh: 我只希望她快乐、有思想、好奇和善良。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the Montessori school is definitely doing great at that.
zh: 而且蒙特梭利学校在这方面肯定做得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: They text us throughout the day.

en: Why is this so important?
zh: 为什么这如此重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think people maybe are missing or don't understand?
zh: 你认为人们可能错过了什么或不理解什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: For me, I read a lot of science fiction growing up, and I think that sort of positioned me to think about things in a long-term view.
zh: 对我来说，我成长过程中读了很多科幻小说，我认为这让我能够以长远的眼光来看待事物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of science fiction books are like space operas where humanity is a multi galactic civilization has extremely advanced technology building Dyson spheres around the sun with sentient robots to help them.
zh: 许多科幻小说就像太空歌剧，人类是一个多星系文明，拥有极其先进的技术，在太阳周围建造戴森球，并有感知机器人帮助他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for me, coming from that world, it wasn't like a huge leap to imagine machines that could think.
zh: 所以对我来说，来自那个世界，想象能够思考的机器并不是一个巨大的飞跃。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when I read Superintelligence by Nick Bostrom in around 2016, it really became real for me where he just describes how hard it will be to make sure that an AI system trained with the kinds of optimization techniques that we had at the time would be anywhere near aligned, would even understand our values at all.
zh: 但是当我在 2016 年左右阅读 Nick Bostrom 的《Superintelligence》时，它对我来说变得非常真实，他在书中描述了要确保使用我们当时拥有的那种优化技术训练的 AI 系统在 anywhere near aligned，甚至会理解我们的价值观，是多么困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And since then, my estimation of how hard the problem would be has gone down significantly actually, because things like language models actually do really understand human values in a core way.
zh: 从那时起，我对这个问题会有多难的实际估计已经大大降低了，因为像语言模型这样的东西实际上确实以一种核心方式理解人类价值观。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is definitely not solved, but I'm more hopeful than I was.
zh: 这个问题肯定没有解决，但我比以前更有希望了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But since I read that book, I immediately decided I had to join OpenAI, so I did.
zh: 但自从我读了那本书，我立即决定我必须加入 OpenAI，所以我确实加入了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at the time, there were a tiny research lab with basically no claim to fame at all.
zh: 当时，他们是一个很小的研究实验室，基本上没有任何名气。

speaker: Unknown
en: I only knew about them because my friend knew Greg Brockman, who was the CTO at the time.
zh: 我只知道他们是因为我的朋友认识 Greg Brockman，他是当时的 CTO。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Elon was there and Sam wasn't really there.
zh: Elon 也在那里，而 Sam 并不在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was a very different organization.
zh: 那是一个非常不同的组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: But over time, I think the case for safety has gotten a lot more concrete where when we started OpenAI, it was not clear how we get to AGI.
zh: 但随着时间的推移，我认为安全案例变得更加具体，当我们开始 OpenAI 时，还不清楚我们如何实现 AGI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were like, maybe we'll need a bunch of RL agents battling it out on a desert island and consciousness will somehow emerge.
zh: 我们就像，也许我们需要一群 RL 智能体在荒岛上战斗，意识会以某种方式涌现。

speaker: Unknown
en: But since then, since language modeling has started working, I think the path has become pretty clear.
zh: 但从那时起，自从语言建模开始起作用以来，我认为这条路已经变得相当清晰。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess now the way I think about the challenges are pretty different from how they're laid out in superintelligence.
zh: 我想现在我对挑战的看法与 Superintelligence 中描述的非常不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Superintelligence is a lot about how do we keep God in a box and not let the God out.
zh: Superintelligence 很多是关于我们如何将上帝关在盒子里而不让上帝出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with language models, it's been kind of both hilarious and terrifying at the same time to see people pulling the God out of the box and being like, "Yeah, come use the whole internet.
zh: 而对于语言模型，看到人们把上帝从盒子里拿出来并说，"是的，来使用整个互联网。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's my bank account, do all sorts of crazy stuff."
zh: 这是我的银行账户，做各种疯狂的事情"，这既滑稽又可怕。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just such a different tone from superintelligence.
zh: 与 Superintelligence 的基调完全不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to be clear, I don't think it's actually that dangerous right now.
zh: 明确地说，我认为目前并没有那么危险。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our responsible scaling policy defines these AI safety levels that tries to figure out for each level of model intelligence, what is the risk to society.
zh: 我们的负责任扩展政策定义了这些 AI 安全级别，试图找出对于每个级别的模型智能，对社会的风险是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And currently we think we're at ASL-3, which is maybe a little bit risk of harm but not significant.
zh: 目前我们认为我们处于 ASL-3，这可能有一点伤害风险但并不显著。

speaker: Unknown
en: ASL-4 starts to get to significant loss of human life if a bad actor misuse the technology.
zh: 如果不良行为者滥用技术，ASL-4 开始导致大量人类生命的损失。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then ASL-5 is potentially extinction level if it's misused or if it is misaligned and does its own thing.
zh: 然后 ASL-5 是潜在灭绝级别的，如果它被滥用或者如果它 misaligned 并做自己的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've testified to Congress about how models can do biological uplift in terms of making new pandemics using the models, and that's the A/B test against Google Search.
zh: 我们已经向国会作证，模型如何能够进行 biological uplift，即使用模型制造新的大流行病，这就是针对 Google Search 的 A/B 测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's like the previous state of the art on uplift trials.
zh: 这就是 uplift 试验中以前的 state of the art。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we found that with ASL-3 models, it is actually somewhat significant.
zh: 我们发现，对于 ASL-3 模型，它实际上具有一定的显著性。

speaker: Unknown
en: It does really help if you wanted to create a bioweapon, and we've hired some experts who actually how to evaluate for those things, but compared to the future, it's not really anything.
zh: 如果你想制造生物武器，它确实有帮助，我们聘请了一些实际上知道如何评估这些事情的专家，但与未来相比，它真的不算什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's another part of our mission of creating that awareness of saying, "If it is possible to do these bad things, then legislators should know what the risks are."
zh: 我认为这也是我们使命的一部分，即创造那种意识，说，“如果可能做这些坏事，那么立法者应该知道风险是什么。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's part of why we're so trusted in Washington because we've been sort of upfront and clear-eyed about what's going on, what's probably going to happen.
zh: 我认为这也是我们在华盛顿如此受信任的部分原因，因为我们一直对正在发生的事情，可能发生的事情，保持 upfront 和 clear-eyed。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's interesting because you guys put out more examples of your models doing bad things than anyone else.
zh: 有趣的是，你们发布的模型做坏事的例子比任何其他公司都多。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was I think a story of an agent or a model trying to blackmail engineer.
zh: 我想有一个故事，一个 agent 或 model 试图勒索工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: You guys had the store that you ran internally that was selling you things and ended up not working out great as losing a lot of money, ordered all these tungsten cubes or something.
zh: 你们有过一个内部经营的商店，卖给你们东西，结果最终效果不佳，亏了很多钱，订购了所有这些钨块之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is part of that just making sure people are aware of what is possible, just it makes you look bad, right?
zh: 其中一部分原因是不是只是确保人们知道什么是可能的，这会让你们看起来很糟糕，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, oh, our model's messing up in all these different ways.
zh: 就像是，哦，我们的模型在所有这些不同的方面出错。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the thinking of just sharing all the stories that other companies don't?
zh: 分享其他公司不分享的故事，你们的想法是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean I think there's a traditional mindset where it makes us look bad, but I think if you talk to policymakers, they really appreciate this kind of thing because they feel like we're giving them the straight talk and that's what we strive to do, that they can trust us, that we're not going to paper things over or sugarcoat things.
zh: 是的，我认为有一种传统的心态，认为这让我们看起来很糟糕，但我认为如果你与政策制定者交谈，他们真的很感激这类事情，因为他们觉得我们在给他们坦诚的谈话，这也是我们努力做的，他们可以信任我们，我们不会掩盖事情或粉饰太平。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's been really encouraging.
zh: 这一直是非常令人鼓舞的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think for the blackmail thing, it blew up in the news in a weird way where people were like, "Oh, Claude's going to blackmail you in a real life scenario."
zh: 是的，关于勒索这件事，它在新闻中以一种奇怪的方式爆了，人们像是说，“哦，Claude 会在现实生活场景中勒索你。”

speaker: Unknown
en: But it was a very specific laboratory setting that this kind of thing gets investigated in.
zh: 但那是一个正在调查这类事情的具体实验室环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's generally our take of let's have the best models so that we can exercise them in laboratory settings where it's safe and understand what the actual risks are, rather than trying to turn a blind eye and say, "Well, it'll probably be fine."
zh: 我认为这通常也是我们的观点，让我们拥有最好的模型，以便我们可以在安全的实验室环境中对它们进行测试，并了解实际的风险是什么，而不是试图视而不见并说，“嗯，大概会没事的。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then let the bad thing happen in the wild.
zh: 然后让坏事在野外发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the criticisms you guys get is that you do this to kind of differentiate or raise money to create headlines.
zh: 你们受到的批评之一是，你们这样做是为了区分自己或为了筹集资金来制造头条新闻。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, oh, they're just over there dooming glooming us about where the future is heading.
zh: 就像是，哦，他们只是在那边末日论调我们对未来走向感到悲观。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the other hand, Mike Krieger was on the podcast and he shared how every prediction Dario's had about the progress AI is going to have is just spot on year after year and he's predicting 2027, 28 AGI, something like that so these things start to get real.
zh: 另一方面，Mike Krieger 上过这个播客，他分享了 Dario 对 AI 进展的每一个预测年复一年都完全正确，他预测 2027、28 年 AGI 之类的东西，所以这些事情开始变得真实。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess, what's your response to folks that are just like, "Ah, these guys are just trying to scare us all just to get attention?"
zh: 我想问，对于那些只是说，“啊，这些人只是想吓唬我们以获得关注”的人，你们有什么回应？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think part of why we publish these things is we want other labs to be aware of the risks.
zh: 我认为我们发布这些东西的部分原因是我们希望其他实验室意识到这些风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yes, there could be a narrative of we're doing it for attention, but honestly from a attention grabbing thing, I think there is a lot of other stuff we could be doing that would be more attention grabbing if we didn't actually care about safety.
zh: 是的，可能会有一种说法是为了关注而这样做，但老实说从吸引关注的角度来看，如果我们真的不关心安全，我们可以做很多其他的事情，那些事情会更吸引眼球。

speaker: Unknown
en: A tiny example of this is we published a computer using agent reference implementation in our API only because when we built a prototype of a consumer application for this, we couldn't figure out how to meet the safety bar that we felt was needed for people to trust it and for it not to do bad things.
zh: 这方面的一个小例子是，我们在 API 中发布了一个计算机使用智能体的参考实现，只是因为当我们为此构建一个消费者应用程序的原型时，我们无法弄清楚如何达到我们认为人们信任它所需的安全标准，以及它不做坏事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are definitely safe ways to use the API version that we're seeing a lot of companies use for automated software testing, for example, in a safe way.
zh: 肯定有安全的方法可以使用 API 版本，我们看到很多公司用于自动化软件测试，例如，以安全的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We could have gone out and hyped that up and said, "Oh my God, Claude can use your computer and everybody should do this today."
zh: 我们本可以出去炒作这个并说，“天哪，Claude 可以使用你的电脑，每个人都应该今天就做这个。”

speaker: Unknown
en: But we were like, "It's just not ready and we're going to hold it back till it's ready."
zh: 但我们想，“它还没准备好，我们要把它保留直到准备好。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I think from a hype standpoint, our actions show otherwise.
zh: 我认为从炒作的角度来看，我们的行动表明并非如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: From a Doomer perspective, it's a good question.
zh: 从末日论者的角度来看，这是一个很好的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think my personal feeling about this is that things are overwhelmingly likely to go well, but on the margin almost nobody is looking at the downside risk.
zh: 我个人对此的感觉是，事情 overwhelmingly 有可能进展顺利，但在边际上几乎没有人关注下行风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the downside risk is very large.
zh: 而且下行风险非常大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once we get to superintelligence, it will be too late to align the models probably.
zh: 一旦我们达到超级智能，可能就太晚来对齐模型了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a problem that's potentially extremely hard and that we need to be working on way ahead of time.
zh: 这是一个可能极其困难的问题，我们需要提前很长时间就开始研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's why we're focusing on it so much now.
zh: 这就是为什么我们现在如此专注于它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even if there's only a small chance that things go wrong, to make an analogy, if I told you that there is a 1% chance that the next time you got in an airplane you would die, you probably think twice even though it's only 1% because it's just such a bad outcome.
zh: 即使事情出错的机会很小，打个比方，如果我告诉你下次你坐飞机有 1% 的几率会死，你可能会三思，即使只有 1%，因为结果太糟糕了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we're talking about the whole future of humanity, it's just a dramatic future to be gambling with.
zh: 如果我们要谈论人类的整个未来，这简直是一个戏剧性的未来在赌博。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's more on the sense of yes, things will probably go well, yes, we want to create safe AGI and deliver the benefits to humanity, but let's make triple sure that it's going to go well.
zh: 我认为更多的是这种意义，是的，事情可能会进展顺利，是的，我们想创造安全的 AGI 并将利益带给人类，但让我们三倍确定它会进展顺利。

speaker: Unknown
en: You wrote somewhere that creating powerful AI might be the last invention humanity ever needs to make.
zh: 你在某处写道，创造强大的 AI 可能是人类需要做出的最后一项发明。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it goes poorly, it can mean a bad outcome for humanity forever.
zh: 如果进展糟糕，可能意味着人类永远的糟糕结局。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it goes well, the sooner it goes well, the better.
zh: 如果进展顺利，越快进展顺利越好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Such a beautiful way to summarize it.
zh: 这是一个非常美的总结方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had a recent guest, Sandra Schulhoff, who pointed out that AI right now it's like just on a computer, you could maybe search just the web, but there's only so much harm it could do.
zh: 我们最近有一位嘉宾，Sandra Schulhoff，她指出 AI 现在就像只是在电脑上，你可能只能搜索网络，但它能造成的危害只有那么多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when it starts to go into robots and all these autonomous agents, that's when it really starts, like physically becomes dangerous if we don't get this right.
zh: 但当它开始进入机器人和所有这些自主智能体时，如果我们搞不对，那才是真正开始变得物理上危险。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think there's some nuance to that where if you look at how North Korea makes a significant fraction of its economy revenue, it's from hacking crypto exchanges.
zh: 是的，我认为这有一些细微差别，如果你看看朝鲜如何赚取其经济收入的很大一部分，它是来自黑客加密货币交易所。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you look at, there's this Ben Buchanan book called The Hacker in The State that shows Russia did, it's almost like a live fire exercise where they just decided that they would shut down one of Ukraine's bigger power plants and from software destroy physical components in the power plant to make it harder to boot back up again.
zh: 如果你看看，有一本 Ben Buchanan 写的书叫《国家中的黑客》，显示了俄罗斯做了什么，这几乎就像是一次实弹演习，他们只是决定关闭乌克兰一个较大的发电厂，并通过软件摧毁发电厂中的物理组件，使其更难重新启动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think people think of software as like, oh, it couldn't be that dangerous, but millions of people were without power for multiple days after that software attack.
zh: 所以我认为人们认为软件像是，哦，它不可能那么危险，但在那次软件攻击后，数百万人停电了几天。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there are real risks even when things are software only.
zh: 我认为即使只是软件也存在真正的风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I agree that when there's lots of robots running around, it gets, the stakes get even higher.
zh: 但我同意，当有很多机器人在到处跑时，赌注变得更高。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I guess as a small push on this, Unitree is this Chinese company with these really amazing humanoid robots that cost $20,000 each, and they can do amazing things.
zh: 我想对此做一个小的补充，Unitree 是这家中国公司，有这些非常棒的人形机器人，每个 2 万美元，它们能做惊人的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can do a standing back flip and manipulate objects, and the real thing that's missing there is the intelligence.
zh: 它们可以做站立后空翻和操作物体，而那里真正缺失的东西是智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the hardware is there and it's just going to get cheaper.
zh: 所以硬件已经存在了，它只会变得更便宜。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think in the next couple of years, it's like a pretty obvious question of whether the robot intelligence will make it viable soon.
zh: 我认为在未来几年里，这是一个相当明显的问题，即机器人智能是否很快使其可行。

speaker: Unknown
en: How much time do we have, Ben?
zh: 我们还有多少时间，Ben？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is your prediction of when this singularity hits until superintelligence starts to take off?
zh: 你对当这个奇点到来直到超级智能开始起飞有什么预测？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's your prediction?
zh: 你的预测是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I guess I mostly defer to the superforecasters here.
zh: 是的，我想我在这里主要听从超级预测者的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The AI 2027 report is probably the best one right now.
zh: AI 2027 报告可能是目前最好的一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Although ironically, their forecast is now 2028, and they didn't want to change the name of the thing-
zh: 虽然具有讽刺意味的是，他们现在的预测是 2028 年，而且他们不想改变这个东西的名字——

speaker: Unknown
en: The domain name, they already bought it.
zh: 域名，他们已经买了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They already had the SEO.
zh: 他们已经有了 SEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think 50th percentile chance of hitting some kind of superintelligence in just a small handful of years is probably reasonable.
zh: 我认为在短短几年内达到某种超级智能的 50% 的概率大概是合理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it does sound crazy, but this is the exponential that we're on.
zh: 听起来确实很疯狂，但这正是我们所处的指数曲线。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not like a forecast that's pulled out of thin air.
zh: 这并不是一个凭空捏造的预测。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's based on a lot of just hard details of the science of how intelligence seems to have been improving, the amount of low hanging fruit on model training, the scale ups of data centers and power around the world.
zh: 它是基于很多关于智能如何改进的科学细节，模型训练上有多少低垂的果实（唾手可得的机会），以及全球数据中心和电力规模的扩张。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's probably a much more accurate forecast than people give it credit for.
zh: 我认为这可能是一个比人们认为的要准确得多的预测。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if you had asked that same question 10 years ago, it would've been completely made up.
zh: 我认为如果你在 10 年前问同样的问题，那完全是编造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just the error bars were so high and we didn't have scaling laws back then and we didn't have techniques that seemed like they would get us there.
zh: 只是误差范围太大了，而且我们要那时还没有缩放定律，我们也没有看起来能让我们到达那里的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Times have changed, but I will repeat what I said earlier, which is even if we have superintelligence, I think it will take some time for its effects to be felt throughout society and the world.
zh: 时代已经变了，但我会重复我之前所说的，即使我们拥有超级智能，我认为其影响也需要一段时间才能在整个社会和世界中感受到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think they'll be felt sooner and faster in some parts of the world than others.
zh: 我认为这种影响在世界某些地区会比其他地区更早、更快地感受到。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Arthur C. Clark said, the future is already here, it's just not evenly distributed.
zh: 我认为 Arthur C. Clark 说过，未来已经在这里，只是分布不均。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we talk about this date of 2027, 2028, essentially it's when we start seeing superintelligence.
zh: 当我们谈到 2027、2028 这个日期时，本质上就是我们开始看到超级智能的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a way you think about what that... How do you define that?
zh: 有没有办法让你思考那个……你是如何定义它的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it just all of a sudden AI's significantly smarter than the average human?
zh: 它只是突然之间 AI 比普通人明显更聪明吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there another way you think about what that moment is?
zh: 还有其他方式来思考那个时刻吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think this comes back to the Economic Turing Test and seeing it pass for some sufficient number of jobs.
zh: 是的，我认为这回到了经济图灵测试，并看到它通过足够数量的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another way you could look at it though is if the world rate of GDP increase goes above 10% a year, then something really crazy must have happened.
zh: 不过，你可以从另一个角度来看，如果世界 GDP 增长率超过每年 10%，那么一定是发生了真正疯狂的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're at 3% now.
zh: 我认为我们现在处于 3%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so to see a 3X increase in that would be really game changing.
zh: 因此，看到这一数字增长 3 倍将是真正改变游戏规则的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you imagine more than a 10% increase, it's very hard to even think about what that would mean from a individual story standpoint.
zh: 如果你想象超过 10% 的增长，很难从个人故事的角度来思考那意味着什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: If the amount of goods and services in the world is doubling every year, what does that even mean for me as a person living in California, let alone somebody living in some other part of the world that might be much worse off?
zh: 如果世界上的商品和服务每年翻一番，这对于作为一个生活在加州的我来说意味着什么，更不用说对于生活在世界其他可能更糟糕地区的人来说意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of stuff here that's scary and I don't know how to think about it exactly.
zh: 这里有很多可怕的事情，我不知道该如何准确地思考它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm hoping the answer to this is going to make me feel better.
zh: 我希望这个问题的答案能让我感觉好一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the odds that we align AI correctly and actually solve this problem, the stuff you're very much working on?
zh: 我们正确对齐 AI 并真正解决这个问题的几率有多大，就是你正在非常努力地解决的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a really hard question.
zh: 这是一个非常难的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's really wide error bars.
zh: 而且确实有很宽的误差范围。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anthropic has this blog post called Our Theory of Change or something like that, and it describes three different worlds, which is how hard is it to align AI.
zh: Anthropic 有一篇博客文章叫 Our Theory of Change 或类似的东西，它描述了三个不同的世界，即对齐 AI 有多难。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a pessimistic world where it is basically impossible.
zh: 有一个悲观的世界，基本上是不可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's an optimistic world where it's easy and it happens by default.
zh: 有一个乐观的世界，这很容易，并且默认就会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's the world in between where our actions are extremely pivotal.
zh: 然后是中间的世界，我们的行动极其关键。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I like this framing because it makes it a lot more clear what to actually do.
zh: 我喜欢这个框架，因为它让实际要做的事情变得更加清晰。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we're in the pessimistic world, then our job is to prove that it is impossible to align safe AI and to get the world to slow down.
zh: 如果我们处于悲观的世界，那么我们的工作是证明对齐安全的 AI 是不可能的，并让世界慢下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously that would be extremely hard.
zh: 显然那将是非常困难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think we have some examples of coordination from nuclear non-proliferation and in general slowing down nuclear progress.
zh: 但我认为我们有一些来自核不扩散和普遍减缓核进展的协调例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's the Doomer world basically.
zh: 我认为这基本上就是 Doomer 世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a company, Anthropic doesn't have evidence that we're actually in that world yet, in fact, it seems like our alignment techniques are working.
zh: 作为一家公司，Anthropic 没有证据表明我们实际上处于那个世界，事实上，似乎我们的对齐技术正在起作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: At least the prior on that is updating to be less likely.
zh: 至少关于这一点的先验概率正在更新，变得不太可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the optimistic world, we're basically done, and our main job is to accelerate progress and to deliver the benefits to people.
zh: 在乐观的世界里，我们基本上已经完成了，我们的主要工作是加速进步并将利益带给人们。

speaker: Unknown
en: But again, I think actually the evidence points against that world as well where we've seen evidence in the wild of deceptive alignment, for example, where the model will appear to be aligned but actually have some ulterior motive that it's trying to carry out in our laboratory settings.
zh: 但同样，我认为实际上证据也指向反对那个世界，因为我们在野外看到了欺骗性对齐的证据，例如，模型看起来是对齐的，但实际上有一些潜在的动机，它试图在我们的实验室环境中执行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think the world we're most likely in is this middle where alignment research actually does really matter.
zh: 所以我认为我们最可能处于的世界是这个中间地带，对齐研究实际上真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we just do sort of the economically maximizing set of actions, then things will not go well.
zh: 如果我们只是做某种经济最大化的一套行动，那么事情就不会顺利进行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether it's an X risk or just produces bad outcomes, I think is a bigger question.
zh: 无论是 X 风险还是仅仅产生糟糕的结果，我认为是一个更大的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Taking it from that standpoint, I guess to state a thing about forecasting, people who haven't studied forecasting are bad at forecasting anything that's less than a 10% probability of happening.
zh: 从这个角度来看，我想陈述一下关于预测的事情，没有研究过预测的人不擅长预测任何发生概率小于 10% 的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even those that have, it's quite a difficult skill, especially when there are few reference classes to lean on.
zh: 即使是那些研究过的人，这也是一项相当困难的技能，尤其是当很少有参考类别可以依赖时。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in this case, I think there are very, very few reference classes for what an X risk kind of technology might look like.
zh: 在这种情况下，我认为对于 X 风险类技术可能是什么样子，非常非常少的参考类别。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the way I think about it, I think my best granularity of forecasts for could we have an X risk or extremely bad outcome from AI is somewhere between 0 and 10%.
zh: 所以我思考这个问题的方式，我认为我对我们是否会面临 AI 带来的 X 风险或极其糟糕结果的预测的最佳粒度是在 0 到 10% 之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: But from a marginal impact standpoint, as I said, since nobody is working on this, roughly speaking, I think it is extremely important to work on and that even if the world is likely to be a good one, that we should do our absolute best to make sure that that's true.
zh: 但从边际影响的角度来看，正如我所说，既然没有人在这方面工作，粗略地说，我认为在这方面工作非常重要，即使世界很可能是一个好的世界，我们也应该尽最大努力确保那是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: What fulfilling work.
zh: 多么充实的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: For folks that are inspired with this?
zh: 对于那些受此启发的人？

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine you're hiring for folks to help you with this.
zh: 我想你正在招聘人来帮你做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe just share that in case folks are like, what can I do here?
zh: 也许分享一下这个，以防人们想，我在这里能做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think 80,000 hours is the best guidance on this for a really detailed look into what do we need to make the field better?
zh: 我认为 80,000 Hours 是关于这方面最好的指导，为了深入审视我们需要什么来让这个领域变得更好？

speaker: Unknown
en: But a common misconception I see is that in order to have impact here, you have to be an AI researcher.
zh: 但我看到一个常见的误解是，为了在这里产生影响，你必须是一名 AI 研究员。

speaker: Unknown
en: I personally actually don't do AI research anymore.
zh: 我个人实际上不再做 AI 研究了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I work on product at Anthropic and product engineering, and we build things like Claude Code and Model Context Protocol, and a lot of the other stuff that people use every day.
zh: 我在 Anthropic 做产品以及产品工程，我们构建像 Claude Code 和 Model Context Protocol 这样的东西，以及很多人们每天使用的其他东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's really important because without an economic engine for our company to work on, and without being in people's hands all over the world, we won't have the mind policy influence and revenue to fund our future safety research and have the kind of influence that we need to have.
zh: 这真的很重要，因为如果没有为我们公司工作的经济引擎，如果没有遍布世界人们手中，我们就不会有思维政策影响力和收入来资助我们未来的安全研究，并拥有我们需要的那种影响力。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you work on product, if you work in finance, if you work in food, people here have to eat.
zh: 如果你做产品，如果你在金融工作，如果你在餐饮业工作，这里的人们必须吃饭。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're a chef, we need all kinds of people.
zh: 如果你是个厨师，我们需要各种各样的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if you're not working directly on the AI safety team, you're having an impact on moving things in the right direction.
zh: 即使你没有直接在 AI 安全团队工作，你也在影响让事情朝正确的方向发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, X risk is short for existential risk.
zh: 顺便说一下，X risk 是生存风险的简称。

speaker: Unknown
en: In case folks haven't heard that term.
zh: 以防人们没听说过这个术语。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a few random questions along these lines and then I want to zoom out again.
zh: 我有一些关于这方面的随机问题，然后我想再次拉远视角。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned this idea of AI being aligned using its model, like reinforcing itself.
zh: 你提到了 AI 使用其模型实现对齐的想法，就像强化它自己一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have this term RLAIF.
zh: 你有一个术语叫 RLAIF。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that what that describes?
zh: 那就是它所描述的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: RLAIF is reinforcement learning from AI feedback.
zh: RLAIF 是来自 AI 反馈的强化学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: People have heard of RLHF, reinforcement learning with human feedback.
zh: 人们听说过 RLHF，来自人类反馈的强化学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think a lot of people have heard this.
zh: 我认为很多人没听说过这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about just the significance of this shift you guys have made in training your models.
zh: 谈谈你们在训练模型方面所做的这一转变的重要性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so RLAIF, constitutional AI is an example of this where there are no humans in the loop, and yet the AI is sort of self-improving in ways that we want it to.
zh: 是的，所以 RLAIF，宪法 AI 就是这方面的一个例子，其中没有人类在回路中，然而 AI 正以我们希望的方式自我改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And another example of RLAIF is if you have models writing code and other models commenting on various aspects of what that code looks like of is it maintainable, is it correct, does it pass the linter?
zh: RLAIF 的另一个例子是，如果你有模型编写代码，而其他模型评论该代码的各个方面，比如它是否可维护，它是否正确，它是否通过 linter？

speaker: Unknown
en: Things like that.
zh: 诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: That also could be included in RLAIF.
zh: 那也可以包括在 RLAIF 中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the idea here is that if models can self-improve, then it's a lot more scalable than finding a lot of humans.
zh: 这里的想法是，如果模型可以自我改进，那么比找很多人更具可扩展性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ultimately, people think about this as probably going to hit a wall because if the model isn't good enough to see its own mistakes, then how could it improve?
zh: 最终，人们认为这可能会遇到瓶颈，因为如果模型不够好，看不到自己的错误，那么它怎么能改进？

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, if you read the AI 2027 story, there's a lot of risk of if the model is in a box trying to improve itself, then it could go completely off the rails and have these secret goals like resource accumulation and power seeking and resistance to shut down that you really don't want in a very powerful model.
zh: 此外，如果你阅读 AI 2027 的故事，如果模型在一个盒子里试图自我改进，会有很大的风险可能会完全脱轨，并拥有这些秘密目标，比如资源积累、寻求权力和抵抗关闭，这些你在一个非常强大的模型中不想要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've actually seen that in some of our experiments in laboratory settings.
zh: 我们实际上已经在实验室环境中的一些实验中看到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you do recursive self-improvement and make sure it's aligned at the same time?
zh: 你如何进行递归自我改进并确保它同时对齐？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's the name of the game.
zh: 我认为这就是关键所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: To me, it just nets out to how do humans do that and how do human organizations do that?
zh: 对我来说，这归结为人类如何做到这一点，以及人类组织如何做到这一点？

speaker: Unknown
en: Corporations are probably the most scaled human agents today.
zh: 公司可能是今天规模最大的人类智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have certain goals that they're trying to reach, and they have certain guiding principles, they have some oversight in terms of shareholders and stakeholders and board members.
zh: 它们有某些试图达到的目标，并且它们有某些指导原则，它们在股东和利益相关者和董事会成员方面有一些监督。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you make corporations aligned and able to sort of recursively self-improve?
zh: 你如何让公司对齐并能够进行某种递归的自我改进？

speaker: Unknown
en: And another model to look at is science, where the purpose of science is to do things that have never been done before and push the frontier.
zh: 另一个可以参考的模型是科学，科学的目的是做以前从未做过的事情并推动前沿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to me, it all comes down to empiricism.
zh: 对我来说，这一切都归结为经验主义。

speaker: Unknown
en: When people don't know what the truth is, they come up with theories and then they design experiments to try them out.
zh: 当人们不知道真理是什么时，他们提出理论，然后他们设计实验来尝试它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And similarly, if we can give models those same tools, then we could expect them to sort of improve recursively in an environment and potentially become much better than humans could be just by banging their head against reality or I guess metaphorical head.
zh: 同样，如果我们能给模型那些相同的工具，那么我们可以期望它们在环境中某种递归地改进，并可能变得比人类仅仅用头撞现实要好得多，或者是比喻的头。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess I don't expect there to be a wall in terms of model's ability to improve themselves if we can give them access to the ability to be empirical.
zh: 我想如果我们能给他们接触到经验主义的能力，我不期望模型自我改进的能力会遇到一堵墙。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I guess Anthropic, deeply in its DNA is an empirical company.
zh: 我想 Anthropic，深入在其 DNA 中是一家经验主义公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a lot of physicists like Jared, who's our chief research officer who I've worked with a lot, was a professor of Black Hole Physics at Johns Hopkins, and I guess he technically still is, but on leave.
zh: 我们有很多物理学家，比如 Jared，他是我们的首席研究官，我和他一起工作很多，他曾是约翰·霍普金斯大学的黑洞物理学教授，我想他在技术上仍然是，但休假了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's in our DNA and yeah, I guess that's the RLAIF.
zh: 是的，它在我们的 DNA 中，是的，我想那就是 RLAIF。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me just follow this thread on, in terms of bottleneck, this is kind of a tangent, but just what is the biggest bottleneck today on model intelligence improvement?
zh: 让我继续沿着这个话题，就瓶颈而言，这有点离题，但今天模型智能提升的最大瓶颈是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The stupid answer is data centers and power chips.
zh: 愚蠢的答案是数据中心和动力芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if we had 10 times as many chips and had the data centers to power them, then maybe we wouldn't go 10 times faster, but it would be a real significant speed boost.
zh: 我认为如果我们有 10 倍多的芯片并有数据中心为它们供电，那么也许我们不会快 10 倍，但这将是一个真正的显著加速。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually very much scaling loss, just more compute.
zh: 这实际上非常像是缩放损失，只是更多的算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think that's a big one.
zh: 是的，我认为这是一个很大的因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the people really matter.
zh: 然后人员真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have great researchers and many of them have made really significant contributions to the science of how the models improve.
zh: 我们有优秀的研究人员，其中许多人对模型如何改进的科学做出了真正重大的贡献。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's like compute, algorithms, and data.
zh: 所以就像是算力、算法和数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are the three ingredients in the scaling laws.
zh: 这些是缩放定律中的三个要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just to make that concrete, before we had transformers, we had LSTMs and we've done scaling laws on what the exponent is on those two things.
zh: 具体来说，在我们有 transformers 之前，我们用的是 LSTMs，并且我们已经在缩放定律上计算了这两者的指数。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we found that for transformers, the exponent is higher.
zh: 我们发现对于 transformers，指数更高。

speaker: Unknown
en: And making changes like that where as you increase scale, you also increase your ability to squeeze out intelligence.
zh: 做出这样的改变，随着你增加规模，你也增加了你榨取智能的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those kinds of things are super impactful.
zh: 这类事情非常有影响力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so having more researchers who can do better science and find out how do we squeeze out more gains is another one.
zh: 因此，拥有更多能够做得更好并能找到如何榨取更多收益的研究人员是另一个因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then with the rise of reinforcement learning, the efficiency with which these things run on chips also matters a lot.
zh: 然后随着强化学习的兴起，这些东西在芯片上运行的效率也变得很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've seen in the industry a 10X decrease in cost for a given amount of intelligence through a combination of algorithmic data and efficiency improvements.
zh: 我们在行业内看到，通过算法数据和效率改进的结合，给定智能水平的成本降低了 10 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if that continues, in three years we'll have 1,000 deck smarter models for the same price.
zh: 如果这种情况继续下去，三年后我们将以相同的价格拥有 1000 倍更智能的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of hard to imagine,
zh: 很难想象，

speaker: Unknown
en: I forget where I heard this, but it's amazing that so many innovations came together at the same time to allow for this sort of thing and continue to progress where one thing isn't just slowing everything down like we're out of some rare earth mineral or we just can't optimize reinforcement learning more.
zh: 我忘了我在哪里听到的，但令人惊讶的是，这么多创新同时聚集在一起允许了这种事情，并继续进步，而不是因为某件事就把一切拖慢，就像我们用完了某种稀土矿物，或者我们只是无法更多地优化强化学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's amazing that we continue to find improvements and there isn't one thing that's just slowing everything down.
zh: 令人惊叹的是，我们不断找到改进方法，并没有哪一件事把一切都拖慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think it really is just a combination of everything probably will hit a wall at some point.
zh: 是的，我认为这确实只是各种因素的组合，可能在某个时候会撞墙。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess in semiconductors.
zh: 我猜是在半导体领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: My brother works in the semiconductor industry and he was telling me that you can't actually shrink the size of the transistors anymore because the way semiconductors work is you dope silicon with other elements and the doping process would result in either zero or one atom of the doped elements inside a single fin because they're so, so, so tiny.
zh: 我哥哥在半导体行业工作，他告诉我你实际上无法再缩小晶体管的尺寸，因为半导体的工作原理是你用其他元素给硅掺杂，而掺杂过程会导致单个 fin 内部要么是零要么是一个原子的掺杂元素，因为它们真的太、太、太小了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh my God.
zh: 哦天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's just wild to think of, and yet Moore's law somehow continues in some form.
zh: 想到这一点真是太疯狂了，然而摩尔定律却以某种形式继续存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so yes, there are these theoretical physics constraints that people are starting to run into and yet they're finding ways around it.
zh: 所以是的，人们开始遇到这些理论物理学的约束，但他们正在找到解决方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've got to start using parallel universes for some of this stuff.
zh: 我们必须开始为某些事情使用平行宇宙。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess so.
